## AI System Builds: funnel, CRM and video production

### 3 2 - Funnel System (2200247217)
- Instructor seeds his assistant with fourteen marketing training transcripts, then builds six reusable skills: marketing strategy, offers, funnel strategy, VSL/page copy, nurture and funnel optimization. Supporting outputs include a brief, funnel map and CRO test plan. The teaching is research and strategy before building pages.
- Demonstration business is a fictional US implant clinic, Smiley Dental. The agency buyer and the patient's buying journey are different research subjects. Research gathers customer language from public discussions and videos, separating vendor promotion from customer evidence. Single-tooth and full-arch treatment journeys differ. Small qualitative samples are not presented here as representative statistics.
- Develop the strategy and script first. Real client facts should come from its website, onboarding information and calls. The instructor explicitly asks for fictional numbers in this demonstration; those numbers are not facts to reuse for DRM or a real clinic.
- Design skills guide typography/layout; a human-sounding writing skill revises public copy. The first output is too much like a general clinic website. He redirects it into a cold-traffic VSL funnel with one primary next step.
- Final page architecture: VSL, consultation request, request receipt, confirmed-appointment preparation, post-consultation decision. A submitted request is not a confirmed appointment. Include mobile, accessibility, form behavior and link checks.
- Deliverables include standalone HTML pages, a twenty-two-email library and automation plan, plus VSL script/slides. A slide preview is not a recorded VSL. Publishing the pages does not activate the email automation.
- Connect hosting through Composio and Cloudflare Pages; verify the intended account and custom subdomain. The demonstration corrects an initially mistaken domain suffix. CRM automation and the email backend are built in the next lesson.
- Some research tool names in ASR are unclear. Do not infer exact tool URLs from those sounds. This review did not publish or alter DRM's funnel.

### 3 3 - CRM System (2200247789)
- Continues the fictional Smiley Dental funnel. Connect Close through its API and Composio, verify access, and ingest CRM training into reusable skills. Instructor likes Close's Chloe voice feature; this is his demonstrated stack, not a requirement to replace DRM's GoHighLevel.
- Plan before implementation and assign authoritative records: Close owns contacts/opportunities; the booking service owns appointment status; staff/clinical systems own consultation and treatment outcomes; payment records own payment status. An email asking to book is not proof of a booking or payment.
- Architecture ultimately demonstrated: Cloudflare Pages serves the funnel; a Worker and D1 event/job records handle intake, consent, duplicate detection, scheduled work and integration; Cal.com owns bookings and Google Meet details; Close is the team's CRM and email workspace. Scheduled maintenance runs every five minutes. The initial VPS idea is revised rather than implemented as the final approach.
- He requests about thirty automations and twenty-two email templates, distinguishing native CRM actions, server automation and human decisions. The workflow is outcome, plan, review, required account inputs, connection, implementation, testing.
- Calendar setup changes materially during testing. An initial Calendly/Zoom configuration reports success but fails when the instructor actually tries booking. He switches to Cal.com/Google Meet, books successfully and checks rescheduling/cancellation against the same lead/opportunity. Do not preserve the first reported success as the final tested state.
- Example calendar settings include a forty-five-minute consultation, four-hour booking notice and fifteen-minute buffers. These are demonstration values, not user-approved DRM calendar settings.
- The nineteen-stage sample pipeline extends from inquiry through consultation, decision, financial arrangements, treatment, healing and aftercare. Staff must record clinical outcomes. Public intake collects contact details and basic preferences rather than a medical history.
- Assign one owner for each outbound message so native Close workflows and Worker sends do not double-send. Example unbooked follow-up is days one, three and seven. Replies, bookings and opt-outs stop chasing. Cancellation can offer rebooking after two days; attendance/outcomes require their authoritative event or staff confirmation.
- Test consent, opt-out during a delay, reply before the next send, duplicate events, booking changes and uncertain send outcomes. Do not blindly retry uncertain sends. Existing test fixtures should not become real recipients. Operational queues surface exceptions and daily/weekly reports.
- AI summarizes replies and drafts responses for human review, with usage limits. It does not freely send every AI reply or make clinical/payment decisions. Clear interest can update an early-stage lead; requests to wait can defer it; clear rejection can close an early opportunity; opt-out suppresses outreach. Ambiguous changes and booking requests create review tasks while the calendar remains authoritative.
- Reply parsing tests include quoted history, out-of-office messages and negation such as 'I do not want to cancel'. Record the source email and process each change once. Replies after opt-out remain visible without restoring contact permission.
- Chloe is configured and tested in a demonstration call with the instructor, including disclosure/recording and scheduling questions. An Irish number is not supported for the intended outbound setup. At the final automation handoff, phone setup and consent work remain deferred. Do not mistake a voice simulation or a later broad claim of automation for verified production outbound calling.
- Instructor conducts a fresh end-to-end test: fictional contact submits the funnel, books a calendar slot, appears in Close in consultation-confirmed status and receives the preparation email. This is stronger evidence than the assistant's earlier self-reported checks.
- Extension: connect Fathom through Composio. Match call recordings using attendee email and booking time; attach the recording/notes to the Close timeline, prevent duplicate attachments and flag ambiguous matches. He creates a test CRM lead matching an existing recorded call and visibly confirms the attached note. He describes applying the same pattern to other recorders or cold-email systems, without demonstrating every alternative.
- Finally turn the implemented funnel/CRM process into an install skill with setup requirements, templates, tests, deployment, monitoring, recovery and the issues discovered during the build. This reusable output is meant to improve subsequent installations.
- No accounts, messages, appointments or CRM stages were changed for DRM during this review.

### AI Video Editing (2200703191)
- Demonstrates video-use from Browser Use with transcription and Remotion. Put raw footage, the intended spoken script in Markdown and real supporting screenshots in one organized folder. Use bracketed asset filenames/cues in the script to identify where supporting visuals belong.
- Prompt for removal of blank spaces, filler and retakes while retaining complete best takes; align the recording to the script and insert relevant proof assets. Specify brand and pacing instead of accepting arbitrary decoration.

Words should appear with the spoken words rather than prematurely. Iterate and compare outputs; a later version with music is worse in his example, so he keeps the earlier version.

He narrows a larger variant idea to six initial tests, keeps a control and places new variants in a separate folder. Feed actual ad results into the next round.

### Reporting Dashboard System (2200247218)
- Build a reporting warehouse between the source platform and the dashboard. Scheduled ingestion writes stored data; opening or filtering the dashboard reads that store rather than repeatedly querying Meta. The instructor warns about rate limits/account restrictions from excessive requests. A schedule reduces unnecessary requests; his wording about avoiding bans is not a provider guarantee.
- Demonstration scope starts with one Meta account, twelve months of history, fifteen-minute refresh, performance reporting and creative analysis. Verify which connected ad account actually has activity. Use read-only platform access for reporting.
- Cloudflare architecture: scheduled ingestion Worker/workflow, R2 raw responses and creative files, D1 cleaned daily facts and metadata, authenticated dashboard API and frontend, Cloudflare Access approved-email login, logs and sync-health records. Plan volume, history, operating costs and refresh behavior before implementation. Prices mentioned are historical tutorial estimates.
- Store replayable source batches. A failed page/import should not replace good data; repeated or overlapping imports should not duplicate spend/conversions. Preserve last good data, verify stored creative checksums and test replay without another source API call.
- Use actual ad previews and distinguish a still preview from playable video. Full video access is blocked by the connected permissions in this example, so a thumbnail-only item should not show a false play control. Creative comparisons should show the whole ad rather than crop it.
- Test access restrictions, mobile/desktop layout, keyboard/focus behavior, contrast, table accessibility, filters and the creative inspector. Inspect actual deployed screens rather than trusting a completion message.
- Initial empty metrics are caused by importing only twelve months while the account's activity is older. Instructor finds activity from July 2024 and January 2025, imports older history and adds an all-imported-history view. Empty-period reporting must be distinguishable from failed data ingestion.
- Dashboard includes campaign/ad filters, spend, CTR, CPA/ROAS where available, creative library, export, source information and data freshness. Reconcile numbers against Ads Manager before client use; the instructor recommends this check rather than demonstrating an exhaustive reconciliation of every metric.
- Add adjustable refresh intervals: fifteen minutes, one, two, four, six or twelve hours, plus manual refresh. Fifteen minutes is described as aggressive; choose frequency to fit the need. A stored history also supports later analysis of winning ads without constant source requests.
- The source recording after approximately 19:43 repeats the latter CRM lesson, including booking tests, reusable install skill, Fathom and reply-status automation. That material is retained in the transcript and documented under 2200247789 rather than mistaken for an additional reporting feature.

### Scraping, Cold Email and Cold DM System (2200268494)
- Connect the sending platform, then explicitly verify access before building. Demo uses Smartlead through Composio. Build source-linked GTM skills from expert training: operator, prospect research, signals, cold email, cold DM, operations and optimization. Trace playbooks to their sources.

Demo chooses established coaching/education companies and one specific problem, preparing coaching-call briefs from scattered context. A hiring post can signal recurring work, not prove intent to outsource. Exclude poor-fit programs or businesses lacking enough recurring work to justify the offer.

Research company fit and current hiring evidence, identify a current decision-maker, enrich/verify their work email and social profile, and keep source evidence. Begin with a fifty-company pilot; valid and catch-all emails are different outcomes. Do not count unresolved or catch-all contacts as verified successes.
- Instructor later expands to at least one hundred qualified companies. A country-name filter incorrectly yields very few companies; using the expected country code broadens results. Final displayed summary reports 103 qualified companies and 105 decision-makers. Record corrections such as country filters, stale jobs, former employees, duplicates and wrong-company matches in the reusable research skill.
- For personalization, research the company and specific buyer, add a dedicated spreadsheet column and retain sources. Christian's imported personalization method ties the company's customers and their needs to a relevant proposed benefit. Do not carry over another example campaign's lead-volume promise.
- First personalization output is weak. Instructor reruns it against the actual README/method, checks ten rows, then applies the better format to all 105 contacts. A useful opener pairs a verified fact with a specific workflow the sender could build. Separate research facts from proposed outcomes.
- Write a three-email spintax sequence accurate to the actual offer. Render it with a real row and assess against the GTM rubric. Revise both sequence and personalization for short, plain, natural sentences. Validate all variation/merge-field combinations before importing.
- Create the Smartlead campaign, upload leads and sequence, read them back and preview several contacts. Preserve blocklist, unsubscribe and bounce checks. The demonstrated campaign remains draft/paused; the instructor's casual 'live' description does not demonstrate launched sending.
- Inbox agent design: scheduled Cloudflare Worker checks Smartlead every five minutes, identifies new replies, loads conversation and offer context, classifies/drafts a reply and sends a Slack review card. Approve/send, deny and edit/approve buttons provide controls. The example moves model access to OpenRouter through Composio; model selection is a demo choice.
- A basic Slack connection does not expose the required interactive callbacks. Create/install a dedicated Slack app from a manifest, configure OAuth redirect and interactivity URLs, add it to the correct workspace/channel and connect it. Credentials are setup inputs, not material to copy into course notes.
- Test approve and edit/approve separately. The first edit attempt fails; the instructor returns the actual error, retries after correction and confirms the edited result. The tutorial states these are simulated sends and no prospect received a message during those tests.
- LinkedIn limitation changes the plan: direct Composio LinkedIn tools cannot save the requested InMail or invitation drafts. He uses HeyReach instead. These are unstarted HeyReach campaign drafts, not drafts in LinkedIn's native inbox.
- Morning workflow at 9 a.m.: select five eligible prospects from different companies, exclude existing connections/conversations, opt-outs, prior drafts and conflicting outreach; refresh evidence/current role; generate/review personalized notes; save the batch and send a Slack summary. The server keeps the list available without the local computer running.
- Live testing catches formatting/length validation and a HeyReach minimum three-hour sequence-delay requirement. Fix, retry without losing saved notes, verify personalization fields, sender, sequence and unstarted status, then inspect the five contacts and Slack links. Despite loose spoken references to sending, the demonstrated final state is saved unstarted drafts.
- The instructor uses smaller-model parallel workers in his own demonstration. No agents, subscriptions, campaigns, Slack apps or outbound messages were created for DRM during this review.

### Content System (2200588891)
- Focus is personal-brand content that demonstrates expertise to potential buyers. It is not the separate mass-generated short-video strategy. Process: research, identify relevant outliers, analyze, ideate, script in the creator's voice, create thumbnails, record, edit and preserve the workflow.
- Begin with the creator's own channel and recent long-form/short transcripts. Map audience, themes, formats, language and performance. Keep different publishing periods separate and flag conflicting dates. An early result demonstration versus a long setup introduction is a testable difference, not proof that pacing alone caused different view counts.
- Save creator-profile.md for positioning/channel context and voice.md for actual speech patterns, recurring phrases, tonality and relationship to the viewer. Use observed transcripts instead of a generic 'conversational' voice. Store a competitor-example shortlist separately.
- Supply a few known comparable creators, then find additional close matches, including smaller channels. Compare a video's performance with its own channel baseline and nearby uploads rather than selecting only high absolute views or old uploads.
- Demonstrated research uses a three-times-median outlier threshold plus a nearby-upload comparison and excludes videos younger than fourteen days. Scan reports 1,140 videos across fourteen channels, 861 eligible and 71 passing both checks. These are demo research counts, not universal minimums. Favor patterns supported across relevant channels and the creator's own results.
- Create five ideas, learn script techniques from source transcripts, and reassess titles after that learning. Retention alone is not a B2B sales strategy: the intended buyer must recognize a problem, see credible evidence and understand the next useful step. Sources disagree about pitch timing, delayed payoffs and hook-writing order; make those format-dependent choices explicit.
- Example selects an AI-assistant tutorial that fits the instructor's existing Hermes series. Script contains spoken narration separately from demo instructions, copy/paste prompts and recording checklist. Proposed duration is eighteen to twenty-three minutes, to be checked against the actual read/demonstration.
- Show the intended useful output first, identify required access/context, build one meeting-prep example, verify its people and sources, save the process, schedule a daily brief and confirm delivery. Label planned/fictional demonstrations appropriately until actually filmed. The script should not invent the creator's routine, tests, client results or prior actions.
- Thumbnail workflow uses real reference photos of the creator plus source training and visual examples. Produce four genuinely different concepts per idea. He adds Pinterest-style references after weak first results, then corrects the repeated hand-on-chin pose by varying position and hand placement in the reusable instructions.
- Preserve the overall workflow and separate research, creator/voice profile, ideation, scripting and thumbnail skills so another client can use the same process with that client's actual materials.
- Editing demonstration uses ChatCut, spelled chatcut.io in the recording. Connect the selected coding subscription, import raw footage and let it transcribe. Ask to remove retakes, mistakes, fillers and dead air, retaining approximately a quarter-second of breathing room between cuts. Historical claims that editing is free should not be treated as current pricing.
- Brainstorm motion graphics and placement before rendering them. He requests a consistent visual direction, some full-screen sections and one head/shoulder cutout with graphics behind it. B-roll is considered and then deferred in this demonstration. Basic tutorials need not use all those effects.
- Add editable controls for text, sizes, offsets, colors and timing. Save an editing style/process for reuse. ChatCut's presets are optional rather than a requirement to install every skill.
- Use clip-selection feedback to target an awkward transition/stutter. Demonstration replaces a repeated 'manual labor' phrase with a clean take and checks the resulting playback. Full workflow ends with recording the script, editing real footage and reusing the approved process, not publishing the first generated draft.

- Course-update example: give the assistant ordered video files, exact naming and description rules, explicit exceptions and which older lessons should become drafts. Upload/save one lesson at a time and preserve the specified introductions/bonuses. This is an example of a bounded operational task, not an instruction to alter Client Ascension's course.
- Ad production: organize actual footage by funnel/ad-set, transcribe each video into a neighboring Markdown file, then use that offer context to plan audience segments, angles and static ads. Use real screenshots when a result is referenced and a supplied portrait when including the founder. Match the funnel's visual design, review outputs and revise.
- Keep file/ad-set/ad names aligned with Ads Manager. Demo static subsets include direct offer ads, founder-photo variants and result-based variants. He discusses later pulling individual creative performance through the Marketing API. That future analysis is not demonstrated as completed in the lesson.
- Video workflow repeats the separate AI Video Editing teaching: raw OBS footage, handwritten script and bracketed screenshot/animation cues, named assets, transcription, removal of errors/pauses, full review and timestamped revisions. Add graphics to improve comprehension without excessive editing. Create a controlled group of variants, organize exports and use the same supporting ad text when comparing footage variants.
- Important completion boundary: the proposed loop that autonomously reads ad results, edits new winners, turns losers off and launches replacements is described as WHAT HE WILL BUILD NEXT, not an already functioning system shown here.
- Automation repair example: broken Chili Piper app triggers stop pre-call messages, Slack notifications and HubSpot cards. Instructor reports the assistant identifying affected Zaps, replacing the broken trigger with a webhook, remapping fields and testing the downstream actions before republishing. Zapier is his preference for visible company-wide automations; direct hosted integrations are presented as another option.
- No Whop checkout, production deployment, ad launch, course alteration or live automation change was made for DRM as part of this review.

<a id="coaching-section-364"></a>
## Ads, Funnels and Copywriting Agency

### What Is an Ads & Sales Funnel Agency? (2189331660)
- Evan Seech describes his agency's paid acquisition work, primarily Meta and YouTube with other channels used where appropriate. Outcomes depend on the offer: leads, booked calls or purchases.
- His central distinction is full marketing responsibility versus only operating Ads Manager. Service encompasses offer/angles, creative direction, pages, copy, backend emails, warming prospects and bottleneck analysis from click to close. Taking the client's sales calls is outside his described delivery.

### What Type of Clients to Work With (2189331667)
- Coach prefers established high-ticket businesses with enough economics and budget to sustain testing. Examples include B2B services, agencies, high-ticket SaaS front ends, coaching/info offers, and higher-ticket local trades such as roofing/HVAC.
- His stated target is roughly $5,000 or more received per sale and ideally $10,000-plus lifetime value. He avoids low-ticket/low-margin examples such as restaurants for this specific service, even though his first account was his parents' restaurant.
- His agency's preferred minimum is about $250/day in ad spend, with a healthy budget that is not the client's last available cash. He cites established $30,000 to $50,000-plus monthly businesses as examples. These are Evan's qualification preferences, not newly approved DRM prices or minimums.
- Allow for testing and sales delays, sometimes fourteen to thirty days before a sale, rather than presenting pixel 'seasoning' as the explanation. Current demand and a strong offer matter alongside ticket size.
- Vet working relationship and stable decision-making. Explain that paid acquisition requires ongoing problem-solving, not uninterrupted wins. Do not accept a poor-fit client only because the initial sale is easy; churn and management burden can erase the benefit.

### Day to Day Operations (2189331670)
- New-to-ads client: choose the funnel based on offer, current situation and budget; build branded pages/copy; outline or script the VSL; client records; agency edits. Research sales calls and feedback for why people bought/booked, current problems and desired outcomes, then reverse-engineer ad angles.
- Add or improve backend email flows, content remarketing and pre-call education. Audit weak sales follow-up and recommend concrete changes to the client/team. Coach's positioning is a paid-acquisition marketing partner, not a button-pushing vendor.
- Existing advertiser: examine seven-, fourteen- and thirty-day-plus data before rebuilding. Find whether the constraint is offer, ad, page, booking, show rate, close rate, AOV or another stage. Preserve working pieces and focus on the bottleneck.
- Daily work is reviewing the entire system's metrics, deciding the next constraint to fix and directing implementation/creative requests. Evan says he spends no more than roughly five hours weekly inside accounts despite many clients, allocating substantial time to agency growth. This is his reported routine, not a universal workload promise.
- Example diagnosis: an ad promises improved show rates but the page promises improved close rates. Correct the message mismatch. If attendance is weak, audit actual pre-call contact and trust assets, not just calendar reminders. He describes calls, selfie videos and relevant resources as examples.
- Rising cost per result with declining result volume prompts his creative-fatigue investigation and new assets from an existing library or new client recording. His simplified fatigue heuristic is recorded as teaching, not the only possible cause of a metric change.
- He cites full-service pricing/revenue share and low churn as his own agency examples. They do not change DRM's commercial terms. Hiring/team implementation remains deferred.

### Tools & Tech Stack (2190192602)
- Funnel builders discussed: ClickFunnels (his preference is 2.0), Webflow, GHL, Framer and Perspective. Prioritize responsive control, especially independent mobile adjustments. His criticism of HubSpot concerns its page builder, not its CRM.
- CRM needs pipeline tracking and backend email workflows. Options include GHL/HubSpot for an integrated setup or Close for sales plus Kit for marketing emails. He considers HubSpot expensive and presents GHL as a workable all-in-one option.
- His preferred application/scheduling combination is Typeform with Calendly as the last step, including partial-submit capture. This reflects his experience, not a requirement to replace existing DRM tools.
- Attribution examples: Hyros for most of his accounts, Triple Whale for e-commerce, Wicked Reports as another option. Research examples: Foreplay, Meta Ad Library and manually saved examples seen on social feeds. No subscriptions purchased.

### What Makes a Good Ad (2190199360)
- Messaging should articulate the prospect's specific current pain, desire, situation or circumstances. 'Calls are booked but prospects arrive guarded or do not show' is more concrete than 'struggling with sales'. Broad avatar labels alone do not supply a persuasive hook.
- Structure: hook calls out a precise problem/desire or leads with actual proof; body explains why it happens and connects the solution/outcome to that hook; CTA explicitly describes the next page and action. Example CTA explains the short video, application and fit call so the transition is expected.
- Direct offer-led ads and longer contextual/educational ads are both discussed. Proof-led/case-study hooks should be supported by the relevant actual outcome. The instructor's sample numbers are examples, not DRM results.
- Visual context should fit the service and buyer. Example contractor marketer films professionally near a truck/Home Depot rather than using a generic info-marketer set. Prioritize clear audio, adequate camera quality and confident delivery. Whiteboards/flip charts can clarify the message and interrupt scrolling.
- Record in the intended platform format: he recommends vertical 9:16 or 4:5 for Meta examples and landscape 16:9 for YouTube. This differs from Daniel's separate landscape-variant demonstration; retain the source-specific contexts rather than invent a single rule.

### Anatomy of a Winning Funnel (2190204123)
- Funnel means the entire ad-to-cash experience: ad, page, backend education, sales process and payment, not only the landing page. Four priorities are congruent messaging, good responsive design, appropriate conversion mechanism and an offer cold traffic wants.
- 'Power of one': write for one avatar, one core message/problem and one solution. His real-estate workshop example improves clarity by centering on finding a first multifamily property instead of simultaneously selling tax reduction as a second central promise.
- Preserve the same through-line across ad, page, email, sales outreach and initial discovery. A message shift between stages can lose the person who responded to the original promise.
- Make design branded, readable and mobile-friendly. His preferred above-fold layout contains headline, subheadline, VSL and visible CTA. Avoid confusing clutter and check the actual mobile load/layout.
- Simple familiar services can use a call funnel plus supporting education. Offers requiring substantial explanation may suit a live webinar/challenge. More elaborate mechanisms are not automatically better; they add friction and delivery work.

### Every Funnel Type Explained (2190208381)
- VSL call funnel: ad to optional contact opt-in, then VSL page, application/calendar and confirmation. Without the opt-in, go straight to VSL/application. Main page can include problem/solution, relevant proof and FAQs, or expand selected VSL sections into readable copy. Test additions/removals rather than treating every section as mandatory.
- Qualified and disqualified application routes should be distinct. Coach fires the chosen optimization event on qualified confirmation only, so disqualified completions are not fed back as the same success signal. Some disqualified prospects end in the form; others have a separate confirmation.
- Low-ticket ascension: sales page, checkout with optional order bumps, optional one to three additional offers, then confirmation/implementation-call option and final booking confirmation. Example front-end prices are $7 to $97, not fixed rules. The product solves a narrow problem that connects naturally to the high-ticket service.
- Consumption and relationship-building matter after purchase. He aims for ascension in seven to fourteen days but notes some buyers take months. Low-ticket funnels are more complex and can complement a successful call funnel when more reach is needed.
- Webinar: ad to registration and confirmation, reminder/education sequence, live teaching, then call booking or checkout. Qualification can separate conversion tracking without necessarily banning an attendee. His preference against evergreen webinars is explicitly his 2025 performance experience.
- Lead magnet: useful free solution to a narrow problem, opt-in, delivery and follow-up toward a relevant paid solution. Strong free content should create trust. He generally adds it when scaling other funnels and when a capable sales team can handle the leads.
- Paid challenge: ticket sales, possible VIP/bump/upsell, optional pre-event call, reminders and a three- or five-day practical workshop. Example pitch on day two with a larger pitch on day three. Usually every other month or quarterly in his accounts; attendees receive practical progress before the paid next step.

### Challenge Funnel Structure (2190379726)
- Walkthrough is a three-day paid virtual multifamily-property workshop. This client runs biweekly, unusually frequent compared with the coach's typical every-other-month/quarterly cadence.
- August 2025 account observation: static ads perform well and the longer page does much of the selling, but statics fatigue faster. He uses individually built static ads instead of dynamic creative after seeing unwanted changes/cropping. Inspect enhancements, site links, browser add-ons, music and suggested-event settings rather than assuming all are off.
- Early-bird/last-chance/date messaging must match the actual event and actual price change. If a discount ends Friday, end it then. He prefers labels such as live virtual workshop/event instead of relying on 'challenge'.
- Page explains dates, daily schedule, included material, methodology, payoff, host, proof, actual guarantee and ticket choices. Heatmaps help identify consumed sections. Checkout includes optional VIP upgrade, details, proof and FAQs; partial contact capture allows later follow-up.
- After optional upsells, calendar invites a relevant call. Backend email/content prepares attendance. A designated salesperson/advisor builds the relationship, helps with resources/replays, checks missing attendance and assists with the eventual sales call. Example bonuses/guarantees are that client's terms, not DRM additions.

### Webinar Funnel Structure (2190379752)
- Example TikTok Shop offer targets people improving an existing effort rather than only beginners. Copy explicitly calls it a free live masterclass, states the opportunity and what will be taught. Date/time, instructor credibility, relevant cases and FAQs support registration; VSL is optional/tested.
- Confirmation page continues education: who it is for, process, realistic questions, content requirements, expected timing and the fact a paid offer will be presented. Include an add-to-calendar action. It is not merely a bare thank-you.
- Backend example has seven to ten automated emails, plus timely manual email/SMS near the event, starting about three days before. Asking what questions attendees want covered encourages useful replies. A capable sales team may contact high-fit registrants and build a connection.
- Content remarketing and pre-event resources prepare understanding/trust. Webinar typically books calls for higher-ticket services; lower-priced products may sell directly. He stays for roughly thirty to forty-five minutes of live Q&A after the pitch. Capacity/fast-action examples belong to the demonstrated offer, not assumed DRM terms.

### ABO vs CBO (2190209807)
- Campaign, ad set and ad are the three levels. CBO assigns a campaign budget and lets Meta allocate it among ad sets; distribution may become heavily uneven. ABO assigns a separate budget to each ad set and gives the advertiser more allocation control.
- Coach normally starts with CBO, including comparable creative across audiences, and uses ABO when he wants to force a specific test/spend allocation or investigate unusual CBO behavior. His numerical budget examples illustrate allocation, not a recommended DRM spend.
- Offer, messaging, creative and funnel quality remain more important in his teaching than treating one budget structure as universally superior.

### Workplace Settings & Style Sheets (2190570217)
- ClickFunnels 2.0 walkthrough recorded August 2025. Import a supplied share link or create a funnel; imported funnels appear in the funnel list. Duplicate a working funnel for reuse. Funnel overview shows page/visitor/opt-in/order metrics and entry points to analytics/settings.
- Master settings: choose the correct connected domain and URL, replace the favicon, select a stylesheet, add funnel-wide base tracking in head code, hide the platform badge and save changes. Generate a share link when transferring a template.
- Connect an existing domain through the registrar/DNS wizard. His registrar preference and criticism of the bundled-domain experience are personal preferences, not DRM account changes.
- Native ClickFunnels opt-in counts reflect its own form elements; embedded external forms may not appear in that metric. Coach often uses unique page visitors from the builder and combines other sources for analysis. Do not interpret absent native opt-ins as proof an external form captured none.
- Products can be physical/digital, one-time, payment plan or subscription; use the payment setup wizard and configure prices, images/tags and relevant availability switches. Instructor notes store/customer-center visibility affected checkout display in his example. Courses can be hosted there, but he generally uses other course software.
- Contacts can be filtered/exported by exact funnel step. Name pages clearly because automation selectors may display those page names. Native workflows handle basic tagging/integration; he often chooses Zapier when the native integration lacks the required actions.
- Workspace settings cover collaborators, domains, email and styles. Build a per-client stylesheet for headline/body fonts, palette, backgrounds, shadows and related treatments to keep pages congruent. No new tools or checkout products created here.

### Basic Landing Page Elements & Settings (2190570348)
- In this builder a funnel contains steps/pages. Instructor sometimes keeps multiple related funnel paths in one client container. The master URL enters its first step; an individual page URL bypasses that entry routing.
- For a built-in split test, send ads to the master URL and set the intended traffic distribution. Sending every visitor to one variation's direct URL defeats the split. Set live status and the correct domain/style/tracking before launch.
- Editor hierarchy is section, row/columns, elements. Use the hierarchy panel to move/select hard-to-reach items. Sections, rows and elements can be saved into client folders and reused; distinguish saving a reusable block from saving page changes.
- Popups need their own desktop AND mobile review. Coach usually disables automatic page-load and exit triggers, using an intentional CTA instead. Set width, padding, background/backdrop, borders and corners deliberately.
- Device icons identify whether a setting is desktop/mobile. Stylesheet presets keep defaults consistent; overrides change a specific item. Save frequently, especially after major sections, because a connection interruption can lose unsaved edits in the demonstrated builder.
- Page-specific conversion event placement is distinct from the funnel-wide base pixel. In this ClickFunnels 2.0 demonstration the event snippet goes in the page footer. Custom styling can be generated with platform-specific instructions, but still inspect the result.

### Live Page Edit (2190570591)
- Create sections, add a row with the needed columns, then place text, image, video, form or other elements. Most illustrated sections use one to three columns. Margin moves the element relative to neighbors; padding adds space inside its container; row width can constrain its contents.
- Text controls include weight, size, line height, letter spacing, alignment, case, links and separate normal/bold/link colors. A global stylesheet edit changes other items using that style; an element override is local. Use intentional contrast/emphasis rather than accidentally applying a global change.
- Visibility options are all devices, desktop only, mobile only and hidden; deletion is separate. Instructor builds desktop first and then checks each mobile section. Where a shared control prevents a good layout in both views, duplicate the section, assign one to each device and edit separately. Copy changes then need attention in both versions.
- Video: use the intended host/embed, inspect dimensions and optional lazy loading, and keep autoplay off in his example. Borders/shadows/corners are design choices. Image backgrounds need enough overlay contrast to retain readable text. FAQ accordion items can be duplicated and customized.
- Button actions matter: open a URL, open popup, submit form/order or another configured action. Native form submission normally advances to the next funnel step; a redirect override changes that destination. Check full-width versus constrained-row sizing and normal/hover/pressed styling.
- Form fields must have the right data type, label, required setting and mapping. Dropdown display labels and stored values are different. Custom fields, checkboxes and selects need deliberate values for downstream automations. His quick checkbox-setting tour is a UI demonstration, not a complete consent-policy guide.
- The lesson deliberately exits without saving exploratory edits to the client's live page. It is not an example of publishing every experiment.

### Quick Page from Scratch (2190571353)
- Create an empty funnel and first page, select a stylesheet, then build an eyebrow, main headline, supporting line, video and CTA. Use separate rows where video/button width needs independent control.
- Tighten excessive default padding/margins, check line-height and above-fold placement, then repeat the layout inspection in mobile view. Add popup fields and assign the button to open that popup if it is the intended action.
- This is explicitly a rough mechanics demonstration, not a polished page to reproduce unchanged.

### Stylesheets (2190571365)
- Workspace settings to Styles is the starting point. Duplicate an approved style, rename it for the client and adjust fonts, sizes, palette, backgrounds, shadows, borders, buttons and corners.
- Select that stylesheet in the intended funnel settings so new elements inherit the client's branding. Local overrides remain possible; the goal is reusable consistency across all its pages.

### Funnel Templates: Import These (2190792424)
- Supplied templates cover VSL call, low-ticket/challenge and webinar paths. Rename steps/URLs, connect correct tracking, set launch status and replace branding before use. Inspect actual live pages on real phones as well as the editor preview.
- VSL template contains problem, solution/mechanism, deliverables, cases and FAQs plus application popup and confirmation education. Replace the instructor's example videos/proof with your own; remove instructional 'delete before publishing' elements and embed the correct form.
- Low-ticket/challenge template intentionally retains example copy and images to illustrate the work. It includes checkout, optional upsell and scheduling pages. These retained product claims/bonuses are not automatically part of the user's offer.
- Some effects use custom CSS, such as turning a strikethrough treatment into a colored highlight. Check copied custom code and event snippets instead of assuming a shared template contains only neutral styling.
- Webinar template supports either a simpler registration popup or a mini-VSL with visible form, with an optional qualification field/routing. Use the pathway matching the actual event.

### Adding an Opt-in Page to the VSL Funnel (2191150419)
- Optional step captures name, email and phone, sometimes one qualifier, before the VSL/application/calendar. Coach likes 'Get pricing and details' as an example CTA. Popup style should match the rest of the funnel and be checked on a physical phone.
- Example retained cold-email copy illustrates sections rather than dictating your offer. Case studies and repeated CTAs support the request; a contrasting deliverables/outcomes section can break the visual rhythm. Test message choices.
- Native submit advances to the next step unless a redirect override is provided. In the shared template the opt-in may sit at the bottom: move it to the first position to use it; otherwise remove it or keep it out of the active route.
- Optional visual test is a GIF preview of the VSL with a play treatment that opens the opt-in popup. The video itself is reached after registration. This is optional, not a mandatory new design.

### Pixel and Standard Event Setup (2190209839)
- Verify the intended Meta business/ad account and dataset. Create a web dataset if necessary or retrieve the existing base pixel from Events Manager. Coach turns on advanced matching in his demonstration.
- Put the base code at the funnel-wide level. Put the success event only on the corresponding completed-action confirmation, not every page or the initial form page. Choose the event matching the action, such as schedule, application or registration.
- Qualified and unqualified confirmations are separate; the example sends the optimization event only from the qualified route. In this ClickFunnels 2.0 setup the event is in the page footer. His statements about other builders are general guidance in the recording, not current integration documentation for every platform.

### WORKFLOW: Funnel Outline & Strategy Agent (2189334699)
- Form captures business/product, niche, ideal customer, objective, price, stage, three to five pain points, differentiation, traffic, existing assets, competitors, preferred funnel, deadline, implementation budget and returning-client status.
- Research agent uses Perplexity to investigate architecture, market/competitors, persuasion, stages, content, offer/pricing, tools, metrics, quick wins and a ninety-day roadmap. Outline agent combines research and inputs into strategy, journey map, audience profile, offer/content plan, optimization, traffic/scaling and implementation framework.
- This creates the strategic blueprint, NOT every finished funnel asset. Feed it into later copy/VSL/webinar workflows and use it to explain the plan to a client.
- Prerequisites: model-provider connection, Google Drive/Docs, a Clients parent folder and Slack. Format to Markdown, create a formatted document through MD2Docs using Docs credentials, move to existing/new client folder and notify Slack. Demonstrated fifteen-page output uses a fictional coaching company.

### WORKFLOW: Funnel Copywriter (2189334692)
- Form supplies client/product details, funnel type and goal, benefits, pain points, value proposition, voice/copy examples, offers, success metrics and returning-client flag. Good inputs come from actual client discovery.
- Research agent combines model reasoning with SERP API search, followed by funnel strategist, sales-page writer and email-flow writer. Each receives preceding research/context. Compile strategy, page and emails into a single formatted Google document.
- Route the output to the correct existing client folder or create one under Clients, then send a Slack link. Connect Google services, Slack, model provider and SERP API before running.
- Demo fictional SaaS output is very long, around twenty thousand words. Instructor still explicitly says to edit for client details and formatting. Generated length/completion does not mean the copy is ready to publish unchanged.

### WORKFLOW: VSL Funnel Writer Agent (2189334704)
- Inputs include client/service, price/payment options, audience, pains, mechanism, transformation, actual proof, offer, any actual bonuses/value, style, length, urgency and guarantee. Retrieve the earlier strategy document and prepare shared context/session memory.
- Generation order: three opening hooks, story architecture, objection handling, closing CTA. Compile into one script, format a Google Doc with client/date, store in the correct folder and notify Slack. Required connections include model provider, Drive/Docs, MD2Docs and Slack.
- Demonstration output includes performance/tone cues and explanatory material and spans forty-four pages. These cues guide delivery; they are not all spoken narration. This workflow explains the long multi-section format the user previously pasted.
- A folder can contain other outputs from separate workflows, but this particular flow generates the VSL script. Actual pages and recording still need production. Optional offer fields must reflect the real offer; DRM has explicitly removed bonuses and deferred showing pricing in its VSL.

### WORKFLOW: Facebook Ad Library Analysis (2189334984)
- Keyword form triggers an Apify Ad Library scrape. Customize country, active status, media type, date and result limits in the actor settings, copy its JSON into the node and rebind the keyword to the form field rather than leaving the sample keyword.
- Example requests up to one hundred ads, waits about ten seconds for the dataset and retrieves it. Filter pages above one thousand page likes, reducing fifty retrieved items to thirteen in the demo. That filter is a sample selection rule, not evidence those ads convert profitably.
- Branch by media: video is downloaded/stored in Drive, uploaded through a Gemini upload session and analyzed; image is downloaded and sent to vision analysis; text can go directly to copy analysis. Configure the required provider credentials in each relevant node.
- Rewrite/analyze using the actual advertised business's context and rules. The sample prompt contains the instructor's business name and must be adapted. Save page ID/name, source URL, media description, summary and rewritten copy into the supplied Sheet schema.
- Long-running active ads are suggested as inspiration on the hypothesis they may be working. Ad Library does not establish their actual profitability. Review the output and source context; the flow does not launch new ads.

### WORKFLOW: Dream 100 Instagram Personalized DM (2189334740)
- Manually curate the target account list, ideally prospects for whom deliverables already exist. Supplied Sheet columns include account, full name, biography and message. Copy it into the user's Drive and bind the correct document/tab.
- Manual or twenty-four-hour scheduled trigger reads the list, Apify retrieves profile/latest-post data and the workflow aggregates it. Analyze image content with vision; the video branch uses the caption rather than claiming full video review.
- DM writer requires replacing the example primary service, calendar URL and sender name, including the name repeated inside the instructions. Save the personalized message back to the Sheet.
- Important scope: these are drafts for MANUAL sending. This workflow does not automatically send Instagram DMs. No schedule or messages were activated for DRM.

### WORKFLOW: Webinar Funnel Generator (2189334706)
- Form includes client, optional strategy-Doc URL, webinar type/date/time/platform/duration, actual bonus if any, replay availability, style, pitch intensity and guests. Retrieve the strategy when provided; otherwise use the form, with less context.
- Sequence: write webinar script first, derive slide-deck copy, write registration page, pre/post-event email sequences and thank-you/confirmation copy. Separate documents are created through MD2Docs and filed together under the client, with a Slack notification.
- Script/slide copy is not a rendered presentation or recorded webinar. Replace links and client-specific details and review before use. Demo script is forty-two pages for a fictional business.
- Narration initially calls the thank-you page post-webinar, but the shown document says the viewer is registered and prepares them for the upcoming event. Preserve that distinction when using the actual template rather than blindly following the initial label.

### WORKFLOW: Static Ad Generator (2189334976)
- Form collects company/service/site, target buyer, benefits, brand style/colors and returning-client status. Concept agent uses these inputs and SERP search, producing three structured concepts with framework, headline, supporting copy, CTA and image prompt.
- Split the three prompts and generate three image variants, then upload into the existing/new client Drive folder. Slack completion notification is optional in the shown flow. Aspect ratio/resolution can be changed for the intended use.
- GPT Image 1 is the model used at recording time; the instructor mentions a possible future alternative. This is not a current model-ranking claim. Output is creative concepts/assets, not a published or performance-tested campaign.

### WORKFLOW: Social Media Pain Point Scraper & Ad Script Generator (2189335071)
- Form supplies topic/product, business description, audience, client, returning status and discussion/source URL. Research combines Reddit and broader search tools, structures findings and passes them to analysis, then a writer produces three ad scripts.
- Reddit connection demonstration creates a web app with the workflow's OAuth redirect, then binds client ID/secret. Setup details are historical and may change. Query terms can be model-selected. The shown search expands to all Reddit rather than only the input subreddit, with a ten-post limit that can still produce long context.
- A larger-context fallback model handles oversized research. Sample research output describes source/sample metadata, engagement, period, recurring pains, emotional triggers and requirements. Preserve source/sample limits instead of treating an AI frequency label as market-wide evidence.
- Three demonstrated frameworks: villain/hero, PAS and before-after-bridge. Include visual cues, format a Google Doc, file it under the client and send a Slack link. The sample app, unlimited-use claims and trial are fictional output examples, not verified DRM claims.

### WORKFLOW: Landing Page CRO Analyzer (2189335041)
- Inputs: client, page URL, funnel type, niche, known current metrics and returning status. Unknown metrics can remain blank/unknown instead of invented. Download HTML, convert to Markdown and combine it with the form context for analysis; optional Perplexity research supplements it.
- Output: executive summary, potential high-impact changes, copy suggestions, testing/implementation roadmap, risks and monitoring. Example suggestions include headline/CTA, proof placement and form text. A suggested timer in an AI example is not evidence an actual deadline exists.
- Format/store the Google Doc and notify Slack. This is a proposed CRO review of page content, not a live split-test result or proof of a measured uplift. The shown HTML-to-Markdown analysis should not be misrepresented as a full visual/device audit.

### Introduction to AI Copywriting (2191106139)
- Daniel presents AI copywriting as an iterative fulfillment process, not a one-prompt finished asset. His claimed reduction from roughly eighty hours to a few hours is his experience, not a delivery guarantee.
- Build context from business instructions, research, actual offer details and useful examples. There is no single correct prompt. When asking for help, supply the prompt, output and desired improvement. Asking a model to draft a prompt is itself demonstrated.
- Copy generation and data-transfer automation are different jobs. Pages, VSLs, ads and emails still need review and revision. His description of all AI products as wrappers and his comparisons of document-reading behavior are the instructor's explanation/opinion at recording time, not verified universal architecture facts.
- Manus is the demonstrated agent. Explicitly instruct it to read all supplied files. A failed attempt to access another Manus conversation demonstrates that cross-chat knowledge must not be assumed; provide the information again when unavailable.
- Demonstrated VSL request includes the actual offer, researched pains/benefits, proof or an explicit statement that none exists, process, timeline and guarantee. Request several hooks and adjust length. Avoid adding unrelated follow-up deliverables to an already large task.
- Export the reviewed script to a document/PDF, import to Gamma, preserve text and separate cards. Remove narration/stage directions from visible slides and inspect the design. This is a capabilities demonstration, not a requirement that every VSL follow this exact production path. Linked example conversations are separate resources.

### Automated Market Research, With and Without Sales Calls (2191127726)
- Research supplies the foundation for all subsequent funnel copy. Prefer transcripts of closed sales calls when available. Read every file and distinguish prospect statements from the salesperson's pitch.
- Produce four outputs: audience pains/questions/concerns and desires; a clear unique value proposition; actual unique benefits, with proposed additions labeled; and a persuasive sales argument based on those findings.
- Separate stated evidence from inferred or latent desires. Explain confidence and reasoning. External research can supplement sparse calls, but identify what was added and why. Do not invent internal facts, data, credentials or customer statements.
- The long role prompt describes a skilled direct-response researcher. Its persona credentials are prompt framing, not real credentials of the model. If a long prompt becomes a text attachment, explicitly identify it as the instruction file among the source files and confirm recognition.
- Demonstration segments include founders, hired growth consultants and internal leaders struggling with manual prospecting, inconsistent DIY and previous agency experiences. They are the sample business's research, not automatically DRM's market findings.
- Without calls, describe the real offer and ask for independent market research rather than repetition of the owner's assumptions. Label the weaker direct-customer evidence. Inspect the exported research document and reuse it as context for sales pages, VSLs, ads and emails, preferably in the same conversation or by providing the full document again.

### AI Sales Page Copy (2191242642)
- Use the same research conversation or supply the research and call transcripts again. The source provides B2B, B2C and adaptive structures, with execution rules, voice guidelines and output formats. Read and customize the actual prompts rather than treating their example facts as your offer.
- Supply real case studies when available. Explicit instruction: remove proof/case-study sections when proof is absent. For high-ticket or sales-call funnels, remove price disclosure; retain pricing for low-ticket purchase funnels.
- Optional second prompt turns the copy into a live landing-page mockup. Iterate individual elements and share the URL with a designer. A mockup is a design aid, not evidence the conversion flow or claims are validated. Platforms shown include Manus, ClickFunnels, Framer, Webflow and Vercel.

### AI VSL Scripts, Gamma and Talking Head (2191249782)
- Preserve market-research context. Edit source-file labels in the prompt to match the files actually provided. Read the mega-prompts and correct inaccurate offer details and missing/invented proof in their outputs.
- Gamma route: generate slide-by-slide copy for both narrated landing-page screen recording and a live sales deck. Import text/document into Gamma, choose DOCUMENT rather than presentation to allow scrollable cards, preserve exact text, switch to card-by-card, choose theme, generate and edit.
- Talking-head route: adapt words per minute to the speaker. Instructor considers five-to-six-minute and twenty-minute VSLs possible; default twelve to fifteen minutes if not testing lengths. His proposed test is short, medium and long versions in separate weeks when traffic supports comparison, not a universal best length.
- Sales-call funnel prompt omits price and asks the viewer to book a call. Low-ticket purchase funnels should instead include price and appropriate purchase CTA.
- Elgato teleprompter is his preferred filming aid. Remove elaborate visual/B-roll instructions if using a simple starter recording. Gamma recordings generally need dead space and filler removed; starter talking-head recordings can use clean cuts and captions, with optional B-roll. The lesson does not require elaborate editing to begin.

### AI Opt-In Email Sequences (2191336233)
- Applies to direct-offer VSL opt-ins, case-study funnels and downloadable lead magnets. Default prompt produces five emails for opt-ins who did not immediately book, but adapt to the actual asset and desired sequence length.
- Ask the model what proof/context it needs before writing the full sequence. Supply actual testimonials or leave explicit requests for missing evidence; do not invent case studies or data. Review generated factual claims and vocabulary.
- Instructor supplies a manually written Olympia sequence as a structural example. Use its presentation of ideas, not his personal voice or sign-off. Provide the client's own writing/speech examples and explicitly instruct the model not to imitate Daniel's voice.

### AI Broadcast Emails (2191336568)
- Broadcasts are one-off list emails, distinct from automated opt-in sequences. Four approaches: trust then strike (mostly value with one sales email); gentle drip (value and light/medium pitch each email); enduring pitch (daily value/pitch plus a dedicated sales email); freestyle emails selected by purpose.
- Sample Monday-Friday cadence is adjustable. His preference for Tuesday/Wednesday pitches over Friday is his B2B experience, not a universal send-day rule. Continue a pitch cadence while bookings respond; return toward trust-building when response weakens.
- Freestyle purposes include pure teaching, soft/direct sales, relationships, authority, replies, stories, pain/solution, community updates and re-engagement. Narrow the prompt when a particular purpose is required.
- Supply a substantial base of the client's own emails, calls, videos, posts, webinars, products or articles. Not every source type is required. If material is sparse, conduct recorded expert interviews; ask AI to design relevant interview questions from the actual offer and niche.
- Do not present another creator's ideas as the client's. Example launch and broadcast emails illustrate structure; instruct the model to preserve the client's voice instead of copying the instructor's style. Linked sample collections require separate reading.

### AI Breakout Videos and Pre-Call Emails (2191337935)
- Breakout videos live on the post-booking thank-you page and address doubts that prevent attendance. Aim around ten, though fewer can work. Generate from actual sales-call objections; if transcripts are unavailable, explicitly adapt the prompt to that limitation.
- Instructor reports variable show-rate improvements, including examples of ten or thirty percentage points. These are source observations, not promised outcomes. Sample concerns include pressure, call value, fit, price anxiety, technical complexity, time, market applicability, scheduling and decision authority.
- A separately accessible duplicate information page avoids repeated conversion-event firing from returning visitors. Keep booking confirmation conversion tracking distinct from general access to FAQs/proof.
- Marketing emails can repeat breakout answers in text and link the videos. His experience favors one or two per day; four prompted cancellations. He describes immediate and twenty-four-hour-before emails, while the shown AIAA example has one marketing email. The prompt generates three by default, adjustable.
- Distinguish scheduler confirmation/reminder notifications from CRM marketing emails. Calendar-acceptance reminders can be conditional. Schedule relative to the actual meeting timestamp so messages do not arrive during or after the call; fixed elapsed delays can fail when booking lead times differ.
- HubSpot is his demonstrated solution for complex time-until workflows. His claim about most other CRMs lacking this is historical, not a verified current product comparison. No requirement to replace DRM's GHL was established.

### AI Video Ad Scripts (2191395918)
- Read Evan's Creative SOP, including its images/examples: environment, presentation, messaging, visual aids/gestures, editing and offer. Supply it within the existing offer/research conversation.
- Demonstrated request: three ad bodies, each with five hooks. Each body represents an audience/angle; splice compatible hooks onto that body and test variants together. Five is an example, not a mandatory count. Opening two-to-five seconds receive particular emphasis.
- Usually film Meta ads vertically at 9:16. Instructor sometimes records horizontal for YouTube, which he treats as a more advanced channel. A selfie recording in an office is acceptable; elaborate environments are optional.
- Inspect generated claims and phrasing before filming. Example campaign statistics and cold-email infrastructure claims belong to the sample, not DRM. The linked SOP and sample scripts are additional resources.

### AI Static Ads (2191522541)
- Start with clear plain text on a simple background, with little decoration. Demonstration uses 1080-square Canva assets, direct offer wording and several variations in an ad set.
- Sample generation prompt asks for three market segments and five concise variations each. Keep text short enough to read. Canva AI can create alternatives, but verify exact wording and edit manually when needed.
- Instructor considers statics useful initially and at low spend, citing sub-$100/day examples; he prefers video for scaling. These are his observations, not a universal limit on static-ad performance.
- His AIAA cold-traffic statics brought lower-awareness prospects and more no-shows than video. He suggests meaningful qualification friction in the form/calendar and observing downstream quality, rather than judging only cheap leads. No ads were launched during this review.

### Building an ABO Campaign (2190209828)
- ABO assigns budget per ad set; CBO lets Meta distribute a campaign budget across sets. Example: three $50 sets versus one $150 campaign. UI labels vary between campaign/ad-set budget and Advantage campaign budget.
- Match objective to outcome: leads for lead acquisition, sales for purchases/challenges/low-ticket checkout. Select website, appropriate pixel and the actual conversion event; do not substitute an event that is not installed on the funnel.
- Demonstration leaves dynamic creative off to show individual ads. Name campaign, audience, batch, hook and body consistently. The spoken example accidentally says CBO while building ABO; settings, not that label, define budget allocation.
- Instructor disables Audience Network, browser add-ons and site links, and generally minimizes automated creative changes after checking previews. Sometimes retains CTA enhancement or overlays. Verify settings again after duplication because options may re-enable.
- Use correctly sized placement assets or inspect original framing to prevent cropped text. He suggests two-to-three primary texts/headlines and one-to-two descriptions, fewer at lower spend rather than filling every slot. Add attribution parameters when used. Duplicate ads for new hooks and ad sets for audience tests, checking all inherited settings.

### Launching Ads / CBO Demonstration (2190209825)
- August 2025 example uses CBO, while instructor notes strategy may change, especially toward ABO for statics. Sample $500/day is this client's campaign budget, not a DRM recommendation.
- Creative roadmap identifies each batch/DCT, with campaign names containing agency, strategy, optimized event and test number. Name media files so the actual hook/message can be traced later.
- Website conversions, selected pixel and Schedule event; dynamic creative enabled. Test broad and a relevant interest stack, plus a previously useful CRM lookalike. Remove inherited interests from the lookalike set instead of unintentionally combining them. Audience expansion may treat interests as suggestions.
- Keep variations limited enough for spend, inspect thumbnails/crops, remove unwanted browser additions, pass UTMs/attribution parameters and verify every intended ad/ad set is published. Publishing from one level may leave other changes unpublished. This review did not publish ads.

### Dream 100 Introduction (2190557296)
- Evan frames Dream 100 as researched, customized free work up front, followed by delivery, follow-up, a call and potentially paid service. He reports growing from roughly $5k-$10k to $40k monthly and winning Gym Launch and Wojo; these are his historical claims.
- Curriculum covers prospect qualification, deliverables, the Gym Launch example, contact methods, follow-up, mistakes, FAQs, KPIs, troubleshooting, scaling and action items. It requires effort and skill, not merely a generic message promising free work.

### Dream 100 Overview (2190557361)
- Do the work before asking whether the prospect wants it. Demonstrate the skill on their actual problem. Asking permission to send a portfolio or offering future free work is differentiated from this method.
- Lower-volume, deeply researched outreach aims for warmer responses than mass cold DMs. Existing case studies, a website or a VSL are not prerequisites in Evan's experience because the deliverable itself demonstrates ability.
- Target respected businesses whose results could establish proof in the chosen market. A subsequent client relationship can create references and introductions. His word 'free' means no necessary ad spend; later lessons explicitly count production and time costs.
- Evan credits Ayman's video as his source. His attribution of the origin/name of Dream 100 is preserved as his statement, not independently established historical fact.

### Dream 100 Process (2190557659)
- Sequence: select industry, list about one hundred desired prospects, research each, identify a need aligned with your skill/service, create useful work, deliver through relevant channels, follow up, book a call, close.
- Find prospects through searches and follower/following networks on X, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn and TikTok. Smaller relevant influencers can have more concentrated audiences than celebrities. Save promising profiles during ordinary research.
- Coaching communities are another source, but the coach explicitly says follow community rules, avoid spam and build standing by contributing useful work.
- His qualification signals: established business, visible web presence, website/landing page, consistent content and existing ads. These are adaptable to the service. Roofing prospects may instead be assessed through reviews, business history and directories. Prioritize the strongest fit first.

### Dream 100 Deliverables (2190558183)
- Match what the prospect actually needs with what you can deliver well. Either start a missing channel or improve an existing one. Examples: thirty days of repurposed posts, cold-email scripts plus infrastructure instructions, a redesigned landing page, replacement thumbnails or usable static ads.
- Make work immediately usable. Scripts without the necessary setup context may be useless to a novice. Provide the knowledge and sell implementation if they want help. Accept that some prospects will use the free work without hiring you.
- Research the specific gap. A large creator with an established editing team may not need generic editing, but may need a precise thumbnail improvement. Avoid treating every visible business as needing the same asset.
- He suggests an optional short implementation/briefing call as the natural next step. His sample ad-performance wager is an example he sometimes offers, not an approved DRM guarantee.
- Two rough paths: money-making, about one-to-two hours per deliverable and one-to-two per day; major case-study prospects, three-to-five-plus hours and two-to-three weekly. Quality and business relevance take priority over hitting a time quota.
- Package in Gamma or Google Docs: short problem introduction, Loom/video walkthrough, deliverable, why it matters, clear next step, optional brief bio/photo and contact details. Visual work can be attached directly to the first message to reduce clicks.
- Do not bury the work in process explanations, jargon or repeated sales CTAs. Treat the free work with paid-work quality. Linked PBD, Gym Launch and videographer examples remain separate resources.

### How Evan Landed Gym Launch (2190558497)
- Exceptional example, not a mandatory deliverable size: roughly 101 pages built over two-to-three days, with a potential introduction already available.
- Assets: email/SMS nurture, seven-day value newsletter, social posts, VSL script, Figma booking funnel, Facebook-group engagement ideas, growth suggestions and lead magnets. Instructions let the recipient hand each asset to the relevant team member.
- Offer implementation help without making every section a pitch. The reported revenue-share arrangements and payments are Evan's examples, not DRM terms or expected returns.

### Dream 100 Reaching Out (2190558633)
- Suggested channels include social messages, email, phone/SMS, communities, direct mail and paid consulting/connection platforms. Research where the relevant decision maker can actually be reached.
- For larger companies, identify multiple relevant decision makers and potential internal advocates. Avoid sending replacement work only to the employee whose role it competes with; Evan recounts sending a funnel redesign to the funnel builder.
- Message structure: specific observation from research, the completed asset, its practical intended benefit, where to access it and an easy implementation conversation. Check spelling and preserve relevant personalization. Sample outcome promises are examples, not established DRM evidence.

### Dream 100 Follow-Up (2190558669)
- Track prospects on a Kanban board: prospective targets, initial deliverable sent, successive follow-up stages, calls and outcomes. Record channel/date and set reminders rather than relying on memory.
- Suggested follow-ups ask whether the asset arrived, offer implementation help, revisit the desired outcome or share a genuine addition to the document. A claim that work was added should correspond to an actual addition.
- Keep identifying relevant needs. Gym Launch initially engaged Evan for copywriting before expanding into other services; the immediate need can be the entry point when it is within your competence.
- Current task is documentation only. No prospect board, messages or client commitments were changed.

### Dream 100 Mistakes (2190558728)
- Avoid long generic explanations before showing the useful asset, weak prospect research, insufficient follow-up, confusing documents and implementation that appears costly or difficult.
- Condense the document and include a clear walkthrough. Each section should help the recipient understand or use the work.
- Evan describes ten follow-ups as his minimum and continuing until a response or rejection. This records his cadence, not an activated campaign or permission to disregard a recipient's refusal.

### Dream 100 FAQs (2190558762)
- Prefer channels where the prospect is active and can personally receive the work. Ask a setter to pass it to the named owner or use a relevant business contact. Once connected, move to the recipient's preferred channel.
- Coach recommends both email and a Loom/video walkthrough. Sample cadence: initial day one, follow-up day two, follow-up day three, add channels day four, next original-channel follow-up day five, continuing with tracked reminders.
- Prioritize highly qualified prospects before medium-fit ones. Genuine interaction before delivery can help when the profile and message are human and relevant, rather than a disguised generic pitch.

### Dream 100 KPIs (2190558817)
- Track controllable output: one-to-two completed deliverables sent daily as a starting example, content showcasing the work and scheduled follow-ups.
- His initial benchmarks: 40% response, 30% booked-call, 50% deliverable consumption and 10% close rate. He reports higher personal closing. Denominators are not fully defined in the spoken lesson; do not silently assume a shared denominator or multiply them into a forecast.
- Count labor, tools, paid access and owner time. Example owner-time value is $70/hour. Cost per deliverable differs from actual customer acquisition cost; calculate acquisition cost using total channel costs and resulting customers. These are accounting inputs, not a claim the method is costless.

### Dream 100 Troubleshooting (2190558869)
- Unseen work: try relevant alternative channels and follow up. Disliked work: ask for specific feedback and revise. Unneeded work: improve research/qualification. Low consumption: inspect relevance, usefulness and sales-heavy packaging.
- Further work for a silent prospect is conditional on its value to you. Unused work can become public skill-demonstration content, accurately described as an unsolicited sample rather than a paid client engagement.

### Increasing Dream 100 Responses (2190558915)
- Coach's suggested options include testing channel responsiveness, office gifts/notes with links or QR codes, calls, digital gift cards, relevant business partners/executives, paid consultations, genuine podcast invitations, events, public demonstrations/tags, LinkedIn InMail, calendar invitations, internal advocates and direct-mail services.
- He also describes burner-account tests and unsolicited calendar invitations. These are recorded source tactics, not actions taken for DRM. His claims that gift-card mail or InMail guarantees delivery/viewing and that persistence guarantees a reply are promotional assertions, not verified technical guarantees.
- Select methods appropriate to the deal economics and contact role. The coach explicitly distinguishes business partners from personal/family contacts. Track channels and results rather than repeatedly losing the history.

### Scaling with Dream 100 (2190558952)
- Suggested progression: early revenue/proof through Dream 100; around $10k-$25k monthly add cold email while shifting custom work toward strong case-study prospects; around $30k add paid ads and reserve Dream 100 for major opportunities. Continue content throughout. These are his staging examples, not mandatory revenue gates.
- Use real niche-relevant results to strengthen future acquisition. If a substantial batch of qualified outreach produces no interest in the free work, revisit research, deliverable, audience and offer instead of assuming only more volume is needed.

### Dream 100 Action Items (2190559015)
- Coach asks students to reserve roughly two-to-three hours daily for ninety days, research prospects, create/send useful work, follow up and seek coaching feedback. This is his exercise, not a change to Brandon's previously stated ten-to-twenty-hour weekly availability.

### Ayman's Dream 100 Training (2190558093)
- Imported training originally made for a content agency. Daniel explicitly says its niche suggestions are specific to that service and should not override the separate niche lesson or the student's actual business. Historical product names/prices and reported growth are context, not current subscription guidance.
- Build a researched list of one hundred desired clients. Ayman initially mentions five-to-ten manual contacts daily, then gives his own five custom short-form videos daily example. Production time and deliverable determine feasible output; this differs from Evan's one-to-two larger packages daily.
- Search relevant business/offer keywords, find a suitable active founder, inspect their website, evidence of clients and service fit, then explore their following network. Expand beyond one tight social circle to avoid repeated prospects. His roughly one-thousand-follower signal is an example, not proof of budget or a universal threshold.
